item.title: OpenRemote — Expression Injection RCE in Rules Engine (CVE-2026-39842)
item.description:

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System OpenRemote (IoT device/rules management platform)
Versions Affected <= 1.21.0 (fixed in 1.22.0)
Language / Platform Python (exploit/detection) targeting a Java web application (OpenRemote Manager)
Authentication Required Yes (non-superuser account with write:rules role)
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

OpenRemote’s Rules Engine evaluates user-supplied JavaScript rule expressions using the Java Nashorn scripting engine with no sandboxing, SecurityManager, or ClassFilter restrictions. While the API layer explicitly blocks non-superusers from creating Groovy rules, it places no such restriction on JavaScript rules. An authenticated user holding only the write:rules role (not necessarily a superuser) can submit a JavaScript ruleset that calls Java.type("java.lang.Runtime") to obtain a Runtime object and execute arbitrary OS commands, which run with root privileges on the OpenRemote host.
